features.title: Base layout
features.description: A table with fixed column widths that scrolls in both directions.

features.title: Library build and package
features.description: Other apps must be able to install the library from npm.

features.title: Rendering spike: <table> or <div> grid
features.description: Virtual rendering of rows and columns, pinned columns and column groups all depend on the DOM structure. Decide it with data before building features.

features.title: Test setup for browser and speed tests
features.description: jsdom does no layout, so layout and speed acceptance items need a real browser. Without these tests, no such item can pass.

features.title: Virtual rendering
features.description: Only the rows and columns on screen are rendered, so the table stays fast at full scale.

features.title: Data pipeline and state model
features.description: Search, filters, sort and pagination must work together in a fixed order.

features.title: Column types and custom cell render
features.description: Dates, numbers and badges need formatting, and filters, sort and export need to know each column's type.

features.title: Theming with CSS variables
features.description: Apps must be able to match the table to their own design.

features.title: UI text overrides
features.description: The built-in UI has its own text, such as "No columns" and filter labels. A public library must let apps change it, for example for other languages.

features.title: Sorting
features.description: Users need to order rows by a column.

features.title: Pinned columns
features.description: In a wide table, key columns such as ID or name must stay visible while the user scrolls right.

features.title: Column groups
features.description: Hundreds of columns are easier to read and use in named groups.

features.title: Hide and show columns
features.description: With hundreds of columns, users must choose which ones they see.

features.title: Free text search
features.description: Users need to find rows without knowing which column has the value.

features.title: Column filters
features.description: Users need to narrow rows by the values of one column.

features.title: Row actions
features.description: Apps need buttons per row, such as Edit, which opens the app's own modal.

features.title: Documentation
features.description: A public library needs docs to be used by others.

features.title: Pagination
features.description: Some apps want pages instead of one long scrolling list.

features.title: Status bar
features.description: Users need to see how many rows match.

features.title: CSV export
features.description: Users need to take the data they see to Excel or other tools.

features.title: Resize columns
features.description: Users want to change column widths by dragging.

features.title: Reorder columns
features.description: Users want to change the column order by dragging.

features.title: Row selection
features.description: Users want to select rows and act on them.

features.title: Keyboard navigation
features.description: Users who do not use a mouse must be able to move between cells.

features.title: Row grouping
features.description: Group rows by the value of one column.

features.title: Multi-level row grouping with totals
features.description: Group by several columns and show totals such as sum and average in group rows.

features.title: Master/detail
features.description: A row expands to show a detail panel below it.

features.title: Server-side data mode
features.description: Support data sets too large for the browser.

features.title: Built-in row edit modal
features.description: Apps that do not want their own form could use a form generated from the column types.
